gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-display: Tube-bright and tall in the middle, Tilt Neon shouts with a splayed c and short ascenders, while Noto Sans Display keeps its own big middle zone. Friendly and level.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-port-lligat-sans: Port Lligat Sans reads tightly packed, its bowls left open on one side and its capitals barely above the lowercase. And Tilt Neon, drawn with one tip, holds a bold, commanding line above it.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-rambla: Commanding is how Tilt Neon lands, its tube-like stroke and splayed c big and loud, while Rambla keeps small letters nearly capital height. Make the heading tiny and it loses punch.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-spline-sans-mono: Spline Sans Mono reads like code, fixed-width and precise, with lowercase nearly matching its capitals. Tilt Neon sits above it, tube-stroked and loud, so the page gets one shout and one steady voice.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-truculenta: Chunky tubes and a splayed c give Tilt Neon real swagger, and Truculenta tucks its rounded, open forms into a compact line. Paragraphs in it would move along briskly, snug but never cramped.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-viga: Viga reads as a plain sans with no hairlines or shadows, its capitals barely taller than their neighbors, and Tilt Neon above it is tube-like and loud. Big, bold and plainspoken.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-winky-rough: Winky Rough reads as a plain sans with a body height nearly matching its capitals, and Tilt Neon's tube-like line never swells or tapers. But over many paragraphs the body stays modest and contemporary.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-winky-sans: A splayed c gives Tilt Neon away at once. Winky Sans, modern and level with capitals barely taller than lowercase, lets that bold tube-like stroke with no pinched joints take center stage.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-alan-sans: Round forms like open parentheses mark Turret Road. Alan Sans backs it with curve tails held well back from the body, and both draw hairline-free, shadow-free strokes that look crisp and modern.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-alef: Parenthesis-round and pen-drawn, Turret Road makes a bold first impression with its flat, unmodulated line. And Alef follows with open-ended curves, modern and clean, so the page feels confident yet easy.
